stem: Pallavi looks at the diagram of three rods of lengths $6\,\mathrm{cm}$, $7\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $15\,\mathrm{cm}$. She asks whether they can be the side lengths of a triangle.

options.text: The answer is $15\,\mathrm{cm}$, because that is the longest length.
Yes, because each length is a positive whole number.
No, because $6 + 7 = 13$ is not greater than $15$.
First construct the triangle with compass and ruler; only then decide whether the sides exist.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Three lengths form a triangle only when the sum of the two smaller lengths is strictly greater than the longest; here 6+7=13 is not greater than 15.

teacher.key_rationale: 6+7=13 is not greater than 15, so the lengths fail the triangle inequality. A names only the longest stick. B treats positivity as enough. D postpones the decision to a construction.
teacher.figure_note: Three separate rods labelled 6 cm, 7 cm, and 15 cm.
